belief: I'm broken and can't be fixed.
origins: Years of struggle and failed attempts to feel better can convince us that we are beyond repair. We may stop seeking help or keep it at arm’s length.
teaches: “He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.” “A bruised reed He will not break, and a smoldering wick He will not extinguish” (Isaiah 42:3). “We have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this surpassingly great power is from God and not from us. We are hard pressed on all sides, but not crushed” (2 Corinthians 4:7–8). “He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion.” Healing may be gradual and incomplete, but you are not beyond God’s care or good treatment.
errors: Believing I am either fixed or hopeless.
Predicting that I will never heal.
Feeling broken and concluding that I am beyond repair.
questions: What has helped, even a little?
What have I not tried yet?
Who could offer fresh perspective, such as a counselor, pastor, or doctor?
What does God do with bruised reeds?
What does “fixed” look like, and is “better” enough?
What small step can I take now?
truth: God does not break a bruised reed. I may be hurt, but I am not beyond help. Healing can be gradual, and I can keep taking steps with His help and the help of others.
hw_truths: He will not break a bruised reed.
I am a jar of clay holding treasure.
God will complete His work in me.
log: Each week, note one thing that helped.
prayer: Lord, I feel broken. Thank You that You do not break bruised reeds. Heal me gently, in Your time, and lead me to the help I need. Amen.
